question: As per Article 118 of the Constitution of India, who presides over the joint sitting of the two houses?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Article 118 of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the joint sitting of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The joint sitting is convened by the President of India in cases where there is a deadlock over a bill between the two houses.
 
• The provision for a joint sitting applies only to ordinary bills and not to money bills or constitutional amendment bills.
 
• If the Speaker is unavailable, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the joint sitting.
 
• This mechanism ensures resolution of legislative disagreements between the two houses of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 118:** It provides for the rules and procedures of Parliament, including provisions for joint sittings.
 
• **Deadlock Resolution:** Joint sittings are convened to resolve legislative disagreements between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, ensuring smooth passage of bills.
 
• **Exclusions:** Joint sittings cannot be called for money bills or constitutional amendment bills, as their procedures are explicitly defined in the Constitution.
 
• **Role of President:** The President of India summons the joint sitting, but the Speaker presides over it.
 
• **Historical Example:** The first-ever joint sitting of Parliament was held in 1961 to pass the Dowry Prohibition Act after disagreements between the two houses.
